proposed.demonstrated_gap:
This is the winner's own 0.160.1 surface compared with the stack's current integration; it is not a replacement. The worker (blueprints/us-equities/workers/native_worker.py at ecfa1127) runs one in-process stdio app-server per run through the vendor's openai_codex Python SDK. Gap-wave2 receipts at SDK/native 0.155.1 already settled new-process resume and a dynamic-tool round trip. They advanced interrupt to status 'interrupted', but the provider-consumption clause is still open.

The installed 0.160.1 may meet two overturn_when needs without a new SDK.
(1) Remote/container worker, which overturn_when currently assigns to the OpenHands SDK. `codex exec-server` is [EXPERIMENTAL]; its `forward` subcommand registers 'an existing WebSocket exec-server as a remote environment'. The protocol has experimental environment/add|info|status ('Adds or replaces a remote environment by id'). This would keep the native Codex loop and move tool execution off the host, which is the limit the gap-2 isolation receipt records.
(2) Multi-client session control. thread/resume, thread/fork, turn/steer and turn/interrupt are stable, and thread/queue/add|list|update|delete|reorder|start are experimental. They are served by `codex app-server --listen unix://|ws://` or by the shared daemon behind `codex agents` and `codex queue --thread`.

The trial uses only the local exec-server forward path, and that path's credential requirements are unverified. The OpenAI Agents API self-hosted path also runs exec-server, but it needs OPENAI_API_KEY with api.agents.* scopes, a separate environment key and @openai/codex@alpha. It is excluded as a paid API with new credentials on a prerelease.

Gap 1's provider-consumption clause stays open natively. turn/interrupt returns {}, and account/usage/read gives only account-level lifetime and daily-bucket ChatGPT token activity.

At rust-v0.160.1 the SDK wraps thread_resume, thread_fork and TurnHandle.steer/interrupt, but not the queue or environment methods; those need its low-level client. TurnInterruptResponse was not read at the pin because the v2.rs path returned 404; the docs show an empty result.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Bounded trial on linux-wsl2 with the installed codex-cli 0.160.1, using the frozen c4 task and the same model route.
- Arm A is the current integration: a stdio app-server with launcher isolation.
- Arm B is the same thread with tool execution in a local container exec-server registered through `codex exec-server forward` / environment/add.
- B takes the remote/container slot if it reaches the same task outcome as A and the gap-2 probe set shows no host-file reads and no host MCP spawns from the worker shell.
- If B fails, leaks, or needs new credentials, the OpenHands SDK remains the reference.
- Session control: one daemon with two clients must show each of the following with typed notifications: resume by thread id from a second process, fork, thread/queue/add delivery, and interrupt. The interrupted turn must end with turn/completed status 'interrupted', and its thread/tokenUsage/updated totals must equal the rollout token_count totals.
evidence: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs#L551-L568: thread/start, thread/resume and thread/fork carry no experimental gate. They use inspect_params because only some of their fields are experimental.

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs#L623-L658: thread/queue/add, list, update, delete, reorder and start, each marked #[experimental].

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs#L1032-L1054: turn/start, turn/steer and turn/interrupt are stable; turn/settings/update is #[experimental].

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs#L1199-L1218: environment/add ('Adds or replaces a remote environment by id for later selection'), environment/info and environment/status, all #[experimental].

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs#L1321-L1325: account/usage/read (GetAccountTokenUsage), with no experimental gate. #L1943 defines the thread/tokenUsage/updated notification.

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/sdk/python/docs/api-reference.md#L70-L90: the SDK has thread_start, thread_list, thread_resume, thread_fork and thread_archive, with no queue or environment wrappers. #L260-L280: TurnHandle.steer() and TurnHandle.interrupt() -> TurnInterruptResponse.

  - thread/resume continues a stored thread by id.

  - account/usage/read returns lifetimeTokens, peakDailyTokens and dailyUsageBuckets, and needs Codex-services auth.

https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference (same index): remote-control commands 'aren't a replacement for `codex app-server --listen` when you're building a local protocol client'. --listen accepts stdio://, unix:// and ws://.

It needs OPENAI_API_KEY with api.agents.* scopes, a separate environment key passed as CODEX_API_KEY, and npm @openai/codex@alpha. This path is excluded.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
This anchors to the Claude arm of open_gaps[1] ('Claude Agent SDK interruption reports usage as unavailable').

At v0.86.0 the adapter is TypeScript and depends on @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.287 and @agentclientprotocol/sdk 1.7.0. It implements newSession, loadSession, resumeSession, listSessions, closeSession, cancel and unstable_forkSession. On session/cancel it settles the prompt with stopReason 'cancelled' and a usage object. It also force-settles a wedged query.next() after a grace period (issue #680).

The usage on cancel is a per-user-turn tally. It is reset on turn activation and summed from SDK result-message usage (input, output, cache read and cache write). So it reports what the SDK observed, not provider consumption, and an interrupted segment with no result usage would be missing. It also sits outside the stable ACP v1 PromptResponse, which at schema-v1.24.1 carries only stopReason and _meta.

Over claude-agent-sdk-python (proposed in round 1, so not re-proposed here) the adapter adds three things: a protocol-level session API (list, resume, load and close over stdio, usable from any ACP client), cancel-with-usage, and wedge recovery. The cost is a Node runtime and a translation hop. The comparison below decides whether it closes the Claude arm's 'usage unavailable'; provider consumption stays open either way.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run the gap-1 Claude criterion through ACP:
- Cancel one session/prompt on the frozen case mid-turn via session/cancel.
- Compare the returned PromptResponse usage and the usage_update notifications with the session JSONL assistant-usage sums.
- Do the same cancel through claude-agent-sdk-python ClaudeSDKClient.interrupt as the control.
- Then run session/resume in a new process and check recall of a turn-1 value.
- Then supply a custom tool as a session mcpServers entry.
Keep the adapter as the Claude control lane only if its cancel usage matches the JSONL sums where the direct SDK reports none, and resume and the tool round trip match the direct SDK.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
This is the closest maintained fit for overturn_when's 'durable multi-host state/replay' without running a Temporal server.

At v2.54.0, durable_exec ships dbos/, prefect/ and temporal/ packages, and the docs list eight engines. DBOS 'runs fully in-process as a library'. It checkpoints model requests and MCP calls into Postgres or SQLite and resumes workflows from the last completed step after a restart. A multi-host setup needs Postgres, because SQLite is single-host; the docs recommend Postgres for production.

Fit limits:
- It runs its own agent loop and reuses neither Codex's sandbox and approvals nor Claude Code's.
- Its openai_codex provider can keep the Codex subscription route: it calls https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex with credentials parsed from the Codex CLI's ~/.codex/auth.json. That shares the native OAuth refresh token with a second client, against the stack's 'native sign-ins left native' rule.
- The models/ and providers/ listings show no Claude Code subscription provider, so Claude needs an Anthropic API key or an OpenAI-compatible gateway through a custom base_url.
- Under DBOS, a CancellationToken cannot be passed to a durable run, and RunContext.cancel() raises UserError. This conflicts with the layer's cancel requirement.
- The docs note that durability is not storage, so it does not answer multi-turn resume; native thread/resume already covers that.

LangGraph checkpointers persist per-thread graph state for continuity, human-in-the-loop, time travel and fault tolerance, which is a different granularity from per-step durable execution.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run this only after a concrete application needs crash-safe replay.
- Run the preregistered gap-11 protocol: kill -9 mid-effect, restart, and require an idempotency-keyed effect row count of exactly 1 while the step executed at least twice.
- Run it with pydantic-ai+DBOS on SQLite and with LangGraph SqliteSaver, on the same task and gateway model.
- Then repeat DBOS on Postgres across the two hosts to test the multi-host claim.
Adopt only if exactly-once delivery and recovery match the Temporal arm without a Temporal server, and a supported cancel path exists.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Targets open gap 2 (native Workflow hard crash, physical-host reboot and remote cancellation are unqualified) and edit ownership. Neither winner keeps durable, harness-independent ownership state. Claude Code agent teams are 'experimental and disabled by default', and '/resume and /rewind do not restore in-process teammates'. LoopX is 'a deterministic (no-LLM) control plane' that sits on the native hosts rather than replacing them. It ships a durable state kernel: goals, typed todos, peer claims and leases, user gates, validated writeback, quota-aware scheduling and cross-turn continuation. Its README says this state stays durable 'across days, restarts, and harnesses' and that LoopX never turns 'an unverified run into evidence of success'. Host paths: Codex CLI `$loopx` drives a visible `/goal`. Claude Code runs `/loopx` plus native `/loop`, gated by the LoopX MCP tools should_run, claim_task and complete_task; this adapter is opt-in and never installed by default, and its own README does not mark it experimental. It installs with `python3 -m pip install --upgrade loopx` and uses the hosts' existing sign-ins, so no new credentials are needed. The only measured data is upstream's own LHTB study: 46 tasks on GPT-5.6 Sol, one trial per task, unequal budgets. LoopX 1.0.3 Heartbeat scored 0.4948 mean reward, against 0.4475 for native Codex Goal and 0.4218 for Plain Codex; strict solves were 7/46, 4/46 and 7/46. This must be re-measured on the stack's current GPT-6.1 Sol. Limits: the product is Codex-first, so the trial should start there. The Claude adapter's --harden gate is 'not a sandbox'. Cross-host shared goals are only a stated direction. Five advisories were published on 2026-08-12, including GHSA-c42j-vw98-9jqm (high): OS command injection through worker_turn_command in the multi-agent launcher, which is this layer's own surface. It affects versions before 0.4.5 and is patched in 0.4.5; the patched versions of the other four were not verified. Never deploy it as a root systemd service.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run the layer's frozen representative task under Harbor or Inspect (never a self-written runner), with equal budgets and at least 3 repetitions, in three arms. Arm A: native single agent. Arm B: the native worker graph (Claude Code 2.1.290 or later with Workflow and subagents using worktree isolation, and Codex subagents). Arm C: the same host under LoopX, Codex CLI `$loopx` first, then Claude Code `/loopx` plus `/loop`. Inject kill -9 of the host mid-turn plus a WSL restart, a peer edit collision on one file, a cancellation, and a user gate that must block. Metrics: turns resumed versus restarted from their prompt; lost or duplicated edits and effects; claim or lease violations; gate bypasses (must be 0); independent acceptance rate; and complete usage (token delta between provider-reported and persisted usage). LoopX is adopted for long-running research workers only if it recovers with zero lost or duplicated edits and zero gate bypasses where native loses state, at equal or better acceptance and usage. It is refuted if native 2.1.290 or later recovers equally.

A workflow can loop until tests pass and hold a human approval gate before the PR, and 'Every workflow run gets its own git worktree'. It runs on the installed Claude Code through CLAUDE_BIN_PATH. The winners already match its validation gate: Worktrunk's `pre-merge` hooks (tests, security scans, build verification) block the merge on failure, and the native Workflow tool sequences stages. What remains distinct is the declarative DSL and an in-workflow human approval node, which matters only under overturn_when's approval-wait trigger. Its README has no benchmark, its 23.6k stars are not evidence, and its default branch is `dev`.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run this once a real task needs approval waits inside a multi-stage worker flow. Encode the frozen task both as an Archon workflow and as a native Workflow script with a Worktrunk pre-merge hook, under Harbor or Inspect. Seed a failing test and a review-blocking defect, cancel one run mid-stage, and restart the host once. Metrics: integrations that land with failing validation (must be 0); approval gate honored across the restart; failed-run artifacts preserved; review catch rate; and tokens per accepted result.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
Symphony is OpenAI's own orchestrator for the surviving alternative, Codex native workers. It runs only through the Codex app-server and has no Claude Code runner. On paper it adds what the winners lack:
- a tracker-backed work queue;
- cancellation by tracker state: a terminal state stops the agent and cleans the workspace, while a non-active state stops it without cleanup (SPEC 14.4);
- per-issue workspace containment, plus a Codex workspace-write sandbox rooted at the issue workspace (Elixir safer defaults);
- optional SSH multi-host workers (SPEC Appendix A);
- absolute thread-total token accounting (SPEC 13.5).

It does NOT close the crash/reboot gap. Scheduler state is in memory by design. After a restart, retry timers, running sessions and blocked approval waits are not restored (SPEC 14.3). The Elixir README says blocked entries are cleared on restart and become dispatchable again. So the 'durable approval waits' condition in overturn_when fails.

The review gate is procedural, not enforced. The agent holds tracker-write tools. The land skill squash-merges with gh pr merge from inside the workspace once checks are green and Codex Review comments are acknowledged. The human gate is a Linear state: the issue sits in Human Review until a human moves it to Merging.

Credentials reach further than the tracker token. Symphony strips only declared tracker-token variables from the Codex child. The push and merge steps therefore use whatever gh credentials the child's HOME exposes; on this host that is the operator's own login, which covers more than one repository. Whether the workspace-write sandbox blocks reading that config is not established here.

The walkthrough-video part of proof of work depends on the launch-app and github-pr-media skills. WORKFLOW.md names them, but the repo does not ship them: .codex/skills at be10a1b79df7 holds only commit, debug, land, linear, pull, push and release.

Linear is not required. The Elixir reference also ships GitHub Issues, Jira Cloud, Asana and GitLab adapters. But the GitHub adapter accepts only open/closed states (github/adapter.ex). A trial without a new account must therefore enforce review through GitHub branch protection (a required approving review plus required checks) and tracker.required_labels, not tracker states.

The trusted-environment warning rules out the shipped elixir/WORKFLOW.md settings (approval_policy: never, networkAccess: true, shell_environment_policy.inherit=all) on any repository where untrusted people can write issue text. Codex's ignore_default_excludes defaults to true, so inherit=all passes every non-tracker KEY/SECRET/TOKEN environment variable to agent shell commands. fp-check rates this a true positive for the shipped configuration, not an upstream bug, since upstream limits Symphony to trusted environments.

The Elixir build is 'prototype software intended for evaluation only', and upstream recommends a self-hardened build from SPEC.md. That build is a separate coordinator decision; this label covers a bounded evaluation only.

Maintenance: created 2026-02-26, so not too new to assess. 24 default-branch commits since 2026-07-08; latest be10a1b79df7 on 2026-09-15.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Setup for a bounded evaluation on linux-wsl2:
- Elixir/Erlang via mise, the installed Codex 0.160.x app-server, and a private scratch repository using the GitHub Issues adapter.
- A dedicated OS user, or a dedicated HOME/GH_CONFIG_DIR, whose only GitHub credential is a fine-grained token limited to the scratch repository.
- codex.command sets shell_environment_policy.inherit=core (or none) and shell_environment_policy.ignore_default_excludes=false explicitly, because the config reference read does not state the inherit default.
- Symphony's safer defaults for omitted fields (reject-object approval_policy, workspace-write), required_labels set, and branch protection on main requiring one approving review and the required checks.

The same frozen task and failure contract also runs on native Claude Code workers (isolation: worktree) and native Codex workers. Cases:
1. Cancellation: close the issue mid-run, and separately remove the required label. The agent stops, and the non-terminal path keeps the workspace.
2. Replay: kill the orchestrator mid-turn and restart it. Record what is re-dispatched and whether partial edits and failed attempts survive.
3. Ownership: no writes outside the per-issue workspace.
4. Integration: no merge before the required review.
5. Usage: Symphony's thread totals compared with the native counters.

Verdict rule:
- Symphony is refuted if land merges before approval, if a restart loses work the native path keeps, or if any step needs a credential beyond that fine-grained token. Check the last point by listing the credentials visible inside the workspace shell.
- It earns adoption only if it passes every frozen case and adds one the native path fails, such as tracker-driven re-dispatch after an orchestrator kill or dispatch to an SSH host.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
RD-Agent is a north-star research worker, not a replacement for this layer. RD-Agent(Q) automates the factor and model R&D loop:
- a Research stage forms hypotheses;
- the Co-STEER Development stage generates code;
- Qlib backtests feed results back;
- a bandit scheduler chooses the next direction.
No foundation worker graph provides that loop.

It fails this layer's 'integrate only after relevant review' rule. The feedback stage accepts results by backtest metrics alone, with no external review gate. The trading catalog's qlib entry already records multiple-testing bias and model cost for automated factor mining.

Fit facts:
- Linux only.
- Most scenarios need Docker usable without sudo.
- conda with Python 3.10 or 3.11.
- A LiteLLM backend that needs ChatCompletion, json_mode and embeddings. Chat can use an OpenAI-compatible base URL. Whether the OmniRoute gateway serves embeddings is unverified; the documented alternative is a litellm_proxy embedding endpoint, which can be local.
- v1.0.0 breaking change: UI_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN is now required even on localhost, and General Model uploads accept actual files only. The token is self-generated, not a third-party credential.

Market fit:
- The shipped Qlib templates default to cn_data, csi300 and SH000300.
- The paper's main results are on CSI 300. It extends out-of-sample to CSI 500 and NASDAQ 100 (train 2008-2021, test 2024-01 to 2025-06) and takes fundamentals from the Wind terminal.
- No point-in-time US-equities qualification exists, and this report does not assert US fit.

A bounded run is a separate qualification unit in research-factors-ml, where Qlib is listed as unqualified.

proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
This belongs in research-factors-ml, once the point-in-time US dataset and baseline exist. Run one bounded rdagent fin_factor (or fin_quant) job in Docker on the WSL2 host, on a frozen US universe and date split, with the LLM routed through the OmniRoute gateway.

Compare it with that layer's frozen non-agent baseline (Alpha158/LightGBM, or the skfolio WalkForward receipt). Use that layer's independent temporal and cost-aware evaluation, adjust for multiple testing across every candidate generated, and record complete LLM usage and cost.

Promote it only if out-of-sample IC and IR beat the baseline after that adjustment and every accepted factor passes independent review. In this workers layer it never replaces the coordinator or the worker winners.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
Superset is the most active member of its class: 1681 default-branch commits since 2026-07-08 and daily releases. What it offers:
- a worktree per workspace, each with its own branch, terminals and ports;
- it drives native CLIs: it detects Claude Code and Codex, and the README says 'Keep your existing agent subscriptions';
- a diff viewer that sends line comments to agents, and a board with Needs review and Merged lanes;
- terminals backed by a background daemon, so running agents and scrollback survive app restarts. In-process Claude Code teammates, by contrast, have no session resumption;
- a CLI, a TypeScript SDK and an MCP server through which Claude Code or Codex can create and manage workspaces.

Owned edits: 'Worktrees separate working files; they do not sandbox processes or prevent merge conflicts'. Deleting a workspace removes its worktree. Deleting a project archives its workspaces and keeps worktrees with uncommitted changes on disk.

Against fit:
- macOS is the supported target. The Linux x64 AppImage is 'experimental and untested', and this stack's main host is the Linux WSL2 workstation.
- It installs lifecycle hooks and command wrappers into agent configs.
- The product has accounts with GitHub or Google sign-in, and organizations (FAQ). The primary Install and FAQ pages read do not say whether local use works without a Superset account. The README's dev setup seeds a dev account behind 'Sign in as dev'.
- Remote access, automations and mobile require the paid Pro tier.

No desktop interface closes any of the five open gaps.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
Xum is a different kind of tool from the desktop cockpits. It was renamed from coder/mux: GitHub resolves the old name to coder/xum, but the README's install link and the mux.coder.com docs still use the old name.

Xum runs its own agent loop ('Xum has a custom agent loop') instead of driving the native CLIs. It offers Local, Worktree and SSH runtimes and a central view of git divergence. With its SSH runtime, it is the only tool reviewed here that dispatches workers to a remote host natively.

Credentials: no new third-party account is strictly needed.
- The built-in OpenAI provider supports Codex OAuth.
- Custom providers (openai-compatible, openai-responses or anthropic-messages, with a baseUrl and an optional apiKeyFile) can point at the OmniRoute gateway.
- Claude models need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or a gateway; no Claude subscription login is documented.

Because Xum replaces the winner's agent loop, its quality on this requirement is unmeasured. It has to be judged as an agent harness, which puts it close to the native-clients layer, rather than as a worker manager.

proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run a harness-level A/B through an upstream harness (Harbor or Inspect), never a self-written runner. Use the frozen coding task with its cancellation, ownership and failure-retention cases.
- Xum arm: Xum v0.30.0, first on the Worktree runtime and then on the SSH runtime to a second host, using the same GPT model through Codex OAuth or an OmniRoute openai-responses provider.
- Native arms: native Codex workers and native Claude Code workers.

Measure pass rate, writes outside the owned worktree, kept failed attempts, cancellation latency and complete usage. Xum moves up only if it matches the native pass rate and adds a multi-host case that the native path cannot run.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
srt enforces no resource caps of its own. The gap-wave2 receipt 4-resource-limit-workloads.json (2026-09-23, srt 0.0.77, WSL2) found no rlimit or cgroup code in srt's 188 JS files. Under srt alone, a 150 MiB allocation and 80 forks both succeeded. Only the outer systemd-run wrapper bound memory (exit 137) and wall-clock time. Still untested: CPUQuota, a disk quota, a cap on the workload's own fork loop, a VM boundary and hostile-workload probes (open gap 4, status 'advanced').

BoxLite's README at main documents what that gap lacks:
- a hardware VM per box (KVM or Hypervisor.framework) inside an OS sandbox, seccomp on Linux and sandbox-exec on macOS (L167, L209-214)
- CPU and memory limits, an allow_net egress allowlist, and secret injection (L37, L167)
- an explicit Windows (WSL2) x86_64 row, 'WSL2 with KVM support, user in kvm group' (L234, L243), the only one among the local microVM candidates, plus macOS Apple Silicon (L231, L241)

New since the last sweep, v0.10.5 (2026-09-30) disables inbound networking by default (POL-647). It also lands in-house KVM VMM commits ('create KVM VMs and register guest memory', 'run KVM vCPUs'), so a trial must record which VMM backend the pinned build uses.

On this host, /dev/kvm exists (Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2), but the user is not in the kvm group. That is an operator precondition for the trial.

Four advisories are published, none newer than 2026-08-26. The record for GHSA-c7v3 (high, allow_net Host/SNI bypass, <=0.9.5) lists no patched version. The previous sweep traced the fixes to #1330 and #1495; this sweep did not re-verify that. Whether BoxLite enforces better than srt has not been measured.

- (d) First-request readiness over 100 cold starts.
- (e) Cleanup after a normal exit and after kill -9, leaving no processes, mounts, VM state or images.

Decision rule: zero forbidden successes and complete cleanup. Any forbidden egress or write, any unenforced cap, or failure to run on WSL2 overturns BoxLite. Promote it only for workloads that need the VM boundary.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
A same-class head-to-head with the actual winner, srt: OS primitives, no VM, both hosts. Two srt defects reproduced on Linux are tied to its mechanism:
- Readiness race. The gap-wave2 receipt 2-readiness-race-quantified.json recorded 8/8 first requests failing (curl exit 7) on srt 0.0.77. Its in-sandbox socat relays remained after upstream PR #257, and no upstream fix was found.
- Silent overlapping-deny write. Receipt 3-overlapping-denyread-write-reproduced.json recorded write_exit=0, the host unchanged, and an ephemeral overlay hiding the directory.

nono 0.79.0 describes itself as a 'Capability-based sandboxing library using Landlock (Linux) and Seatbelt (macOS)' (docs.rs). On Linux it therefore enforces kernel access rights rather than bubblewrap bind or overlay mounts, so neither defect's mechanism exists in its design. This is unmeasured. It is not established that nono can express the same overlapping deny-read and allow-write policy, because Landlock grants are additive. nono's own proxy start-up ordering is also untested. Egress goes through profiles carrying a network allowlist, a credential proxy and L7 filtering (README L109, L133-134, L189).

The trial is feasible now, with no host change. This WSL2 kernel has CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK=y with landlock first in CONFIG_LSM, and landlock_create_ruleset reports ABI 7 (TCP rules need ABI 4 or later). README L94 lists WSL2. The repository was renamed: always-further/nono now resolves to nolabs-ai/nono.

These risks are recorded but not decisive:
- nono is pre-1.0 (README L33).
- It has 12 published advisories. They include network-policy bypasses fixed in 0.74.0 (GHSA-6hww, GHSA-7q3j, GHSA-gcpc, the last a DNS tunnel via the proxy) and a high seccomp x86_64 legacy-ABI bypass (GHSA-vhq2, fixed in 0.74.0).
- Two high records still show no patched release. They are GHSA-8r33 (an L7 endpoint path-policy bypass in nono-proxy, '>=0.73.0: Not yet') and GHSA-wjv5 (a tool-sandbox shim fall-through, 'not yet released'). The v0.78.0 notes list both, so their status is unresolved. Both concern nono-only features that an srt-parity trial would leave disabled.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run nono v0.79.0, with L7 endpoint rules and tool-sandbox shims disabled, and a version-recorded srt on the gap-wave2 fixtures. On WSL2 this needs no host change. Repeat on both Macs, where both tools use Seatbelt, so the Mac half compares policy generation rather than mechanism. Measure:
- (a) First-request success over 100 cold starts without retries, against srt's 8/8 failures in receipt 2.
- (b) The receipt 3 overlapping deny-read and write fixture: either nono expresses it and the write exits non-zero, or record it as inexpressible.
- (c) The receipt 0 egress cases plus IPv6 deny, NAT64 and IPv4-mapped targets, UDP 53 to a public resolver, and TLS SNI/Host mismatch. Landlock ABI 7 has no UDP rules, so record what blocks UDP.
- (d) Cleanup.

nono replaces srt only with zero forbidden successes and no readiness failures. It is overturned by any forbidden success that srt blocks, by a stack policy it cannot express, or by GHSA-8r33 or GHSA-wjv5 staying unpatched for a feature the selected policy needs.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
Gondolin documents the strongest egress confinement for the cases srt's gap-0 receipt still lists as untested: IPv6 deny, direct queries to a public resolver, DNS rebinding (cause undetermined) and TLS termination. Per the security design's Egress Capability Matrix:
- guest traffic ends in a host-side policy stack where only HTTP and TLS pass by default, checked against hostname allowlists plus DNS and IP checks
- HTTP CONNECT is denied and unknown protocols are dropped
- UDP is blocked except port 53
- DNS defaults to 'synthetic', with no upstream lookups, so DNS cannot be used as an egress channel

Secrets are injected host-side, and only for allowed destinations (README L45-46). VM-level sandbox.cpus and sandbox.memory exist on both backends (backends page).

It is not targeted because its own docs exclude what gap 4 needs. The non-goals include 'VM escape / hypervisor bugs ... a QEMU escape is a host compromise' and 'Denial of service ... no complete DoS isolation'. No host-side jail around QEMU is documented, whereas BoxLite documents one.

Its fit on WSL2 x86_64 is weaker than on the Macs. README L114 says 'ARM64 is the most tested runtime path today', and L79 lists qemu-system-arm as the Linux prerequisite. QEMU guests can match qemu-system-x86_64, though, and a linux-x64 krun runner package exists. There is no QUIC or generic UDP (limitations page). It has 0 published advisories, which means none among what was assessed, not a clean verdict.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run the battery's network and cleanup halves on v0.13.0, against BoxLite's allow_net and srt. Cover IPv4 and IPv6 deny, direct IP, UDP 53 to a public resolver, rebinding names that resolve to 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254, TLS SNI/Host mismatch, and CONNECT or SOCKS. Run them on a Mac (arm64) and on WSL2 with an x86_64 guest under KVM acceleration. Add in-VM memory and fork caps with host-side QEMU limits.

Gondolin becomes the targeted candidate if it is the only candidate with zero forbidden egress and its caps hold. It is dropped if x86_64 guests are not KVM-accelerated on WSL2, or if the simulation fixture needs non-HTTP egress.
evidence: https://earendil-works.github.io/gondolin/security/: the Egress Capability Matrix says the guest 'cannot open arbitrary raw TCP tunnels, cannot use UDP (except DNS)'. HTTP CONNECT is denied, and synthetic DNS is the default. The Non-Goals include QEMU escape (a host compromise) and 'no complete DoS isolation'.

https://earendil-works.github.io/gondolin/backends/: sandbox.cpus and sandbox.memory are supported on qemu and krun. The QEMU guest architecture must match qemu-system-aarch64 or qemu-system-x86_64. krun runner packages include linux-x64.
https://earendil-works.github.io/gondolin/limitations/: lists backend parity gaps and no QUIC, WebRTC or generic UDP.

https://github.com/earendil-works/gondolin/blob/main/README.md: read via gh api readme (blob d47a6a08). L8-10 say QEMU is the default with an experimental krun backend. L45-46 describe the placeholder secret injection. L79 gives the Linux prerequisite, qemu-system-arm. L114 says 'ARM64 is the most tested runtime path today'. L120-130 cover the HTTP/TLS egress policy, DNS modes, rootfs modes and checkpoints.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
Docker's own local microVM sandbox for coding agents. Verified so far:
- The v0.47.0 release (2026-10-05) ships DockerSandboxes-linux-amd64-ubuntu2604.deb, which matches this host's Ubuntu 26.04.1, plus darwin-arm64 builds, with provenance and SBOM attestations for each platform.
- install.md says local sandboxes need KVM and the user in the kvm group, but no Docker Desktop or Engine.
- The FAQ documents local 'sbx policy' allow and deny rules for network and filesystem.
- The overview lists GPU passthrough under Configuration, which matters for the RTX 4090.

That makes it a vendor-maintained, packaged path on both hosts, which neither srt nor BoxLite offers. A private Docker daemon per sandbox appears only in a search summary of Docker's docs and blog; it was not verified on a fetched page.

It stays behind BoxLite for three reasons:
- The documented setup includes 'sbx login' (install.md), and the overview says 'Install the sbx CLI and sign in'. A Docker account is a new credential, which the selection rules allow only when a demonstrated gap requires one, and BoxLite covers the VM gap without one.
- The repository holds only LICENSE, README.md and SECURITY.md, so no source pin can be cited for review.
- Telemetry is on by default (the FAQ gives SBX_NO_TELEMETRY=1 to opt out).

The prerequisites I read do not name WSL2. Whether local sandboxes run without signing in was not established.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Applies if BoxLite fails the battery on WSL2, or its in-progress VMM transition breaks it, and the operator accepts a Docker sign-in. Then run sbx v0.47.0 with telemetry disabled on the same battery, using the ubuntu2604 package on WSL2 and repeating on both Macs. Adopt it only with zero forbidden successes, enforced caps, and a teardown that leaves no microVMs, images or daemons.

output.notes:
North-star action: qualify isolation for untrusted US-equities research and historical-simulation tasks. These proposals complement edit separation; no trial, installation, candidate execution or trading qualification was performed.

Current gaps were corrected against the later receipts. The [network receipt](https://github.com/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/blob/main/evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/foundation__isolation/0-network-fixture-extension.json) already records TLS CONNECT, SOCKS5 and remote-host allow/deny evidence. Remaining cases include IPv6 denial, live DNS rebinding, TLS termination and broader escape testing. The [resource receipt](https://github.com/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/blob/main/evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/foundation__isolation/4-resource-limit-workloads.json) leaves CPU-rate limiting, actual disk quotas, a fork workload that reaches execution, and VM-boundary qualification unresolved. It does not establish that every possible resource-control mechanism is absent. Supplied follow-up statuses for gaps 1–3 were respected as settled.

Trial decision rule: use upstream regression suites and an upstream evaluation harness such as [Inspect](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/sandboxing.html), with any necessary provider integration separately reviewed. Hold worktree handling, image/package pins and fixtures constant. Pre-register resource ceilings and output tolerances; require zero policy violations and successful authorized cases across 30 lifecycle repetitions. Record cold/warm p95 latency, peak host memory and residual processes, mounts, sockets and per-run storage. A vCPU allocation is not proof of CPU-rate throttling. Passing bounded probes is not a general escape-proof result.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The installed native client codex-cli 0.160.1 ships `codex sandbox [COMMAND]...`. Its README says 'The CLI surface is `codex sandbox`; the host OS selects the sandbox backend' (linux-sandbox README L111). The layer has never compared it with the winner. On paper at rust-v0.160.1 it handles three open sandbox-runtime (srt) gaps differently. (a) Readiness, gap 2: the managed-proxy bridge waits for an explicit readiness byte (HOST_BRIDGE_READY, proxy_routing.rs L48, L169-175, L345-349, L362-367; error text 'host bridge did not acknowledge readiness'). The README says seccomp blocks new AF_UNIX/socketpair creation 'after the bridge is live' (L85-89). srt 0.0.77 and 0.0.78 start their socat relays in the background, and the fix exists only on srt main (PR #639). (b) Overlapping path rules, gap 3: split-policy entries are applied in path-specificity order, so narrower denied subpaths win (L53-58), and symlink-in-path or missing protected paths are masked with /dev/null (L78-80). srt instead documents a read-denied directory as an 'EMPTY WRITABLE directory' tmpfs that discards writes (srt README v0.0.78 L440). (c) Network, gap 0: weaker on paper. The codex network-proxy README blocks hostnames that resolve to local or private IPs by 'best-effort DNS lookup' and says 'DNS rebinding is hard to fully prevent without pinning the resolved IP(s)' (L249-251, L264-267). srt dials the address that passed its check, with 'no second lookup' (srt README L361). Codex limited mode allows only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS and needs MITM for HTTPS (L253-255). The in-sandbox bridge listener binds IPv4 127.0.0.1 only (proxy_routing.rs L391-404); IPv6 behaviour is untested. Defaults: `codex sandbox` applies the active config's effective permission profile (debug_sandbox.rs L273) and starts the managed proxy only when the profile configures network (L353-373). Restricted network without the proxy uses --unshare-net (README L83-84). Limits shared with srt: Codex prefers the first `bwrap` on PATH outside the cwd (README L10-16). On this host that is the same /usr/bin/bwrap 0.11.1-1ubuntu0.3 that lacks the CVE-2026-87766 fix. The vendored fallback runs only when no bwrap is on PATH; it is bubblewrap 0.11.2 per NEWS.md, and its bubblewrap.c has no openat2/RESOLVE_IN_ROOT (other files were not checked). Resource limits were not found in linux-sandbox/README.md at the tag, so gap 4 is unchanged. On macOS it uses Seatbelt profiles (codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt*.sbpl), the same OS primitive as srt.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run this as a separate qualification unit on the WSL2 host, using the same /usr/bin/bwrap. Re-run the existing srt fixtures (evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/foundation__isolation) under `codex sandbox -P <profile>` with an equivalent permissions profile and the managed proxy: filesystem permit/deny, overlapping denyRead/allowWrite, TLS, IPv6-loopback, SOCKS5 and remote-host network, a DNS name that resolves to loopback, first-request readiness at N>=8 without curl retries, and memory/fork workloads. Codex joins or replaces srt as the native sandbox only if it reproduces every srt deny outcome, shows 0 first-request refusals without retries, and turns the overlapping-path write into a visible failure instead of a discarded write. srt keeps the slot if Codex lets any denied path, host or loopback-resolving name through, or loses an IPv6 or remote-host deny.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The winner's backend has regressed on this host. srt uses bubblewrap on Linux (srt README v0.0.78 L5, L108), and Codex prefers the first bwrap on PATH. Both therefore run the Ubuntu 26.04 package bubblewrap 0.11.1-1ubuntu0.3, whose changelog (2026-09-17) reads 'SECURITY REGRESSION: Incompatibility with Flatpak (LP: #2167621) - debian: Drop CVE-2026-87766'. Upstream GHSA-pxhw-h44j-8pfx is CVE-2026-87766 (high, CVSS 8.8, CWE-22/CWE-59; versions below 0.12.0 are vulnerable, patched in 0.12.0). Per the advisory, 'When bubblewrap creates a file in /newroot it may follow a symlink in a parent that points to /oldroot', which creates files on the host as the launching uid. srt makes bubblewrap create files on content the sandbox can write. PR #618 says 'an absent denyWrite path is blocked by an empty file (mount point) that bubblewrap makes on the host', and README L745 says 'it first creates a mount point there: an empty, read-only file (or an empty directory...)'. That matches the advisory's precondition. fp-check verdict: TRUE that the host bwrap lacks the fix (package changelog plus advisory range). Exploitation through srt or codex arguments is PLAUSIBLE but unverified, since no fixture was run. LP #2167621 comment #14 says the revert leaves CVE-2026-87766 unfixed, that Debian, Fedora and Mageia moved to 0.12.0, and that backporting to 0.11.x is 'unlikely to be feasible'. Upstream v0.13.0 (2026-09-22) adds mount_setattr remounts and rejects empty path arguments. v0.12.0 adds --not-a-security-boundary and drops setuid builds. Neither release addresses srt's socat readiness or its tmpfs semantics, which are srt-level. srt's own tests in PR #614 ran on bubblewrap 0.11.2.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Monty is a different boundary class: an interpreter-level sandbox for model-written glue code (code-mode tool calls), not a process sandbox. The README says 'Filesystem, environment variables and network do not exist inside the sandbox: it reaches the host only through the functions and mounts you pass in' (v1.1.0 L27-28). It claims a new sandbox starts in 'under 1ms from a running pool' (L24); that is a vendor claim, unmeasured here. It documents interpreter-level per-session limits: 'Monty enforces hard limits on memory, execution time and recursion depth, configured per session'. The page's table, headed 'The six settings', lists seven keys: max_memory, max_feed_duration_secs, max_turn_duration_secs, max_recursion_depth (default 1000), gc_interval, max_suspensions (default 1000) and max_total_sleep_secs. Local pools run each session in a worker subprocess spawned with an empty environment. It is ruled out for north-star research code. The docs say 'Third-party packages. There is no sys.path and no site-packages', so numpy, pandas, NautilusTrader and LEAN cannot run. The stdlib is a partial subset of 19 modules: asyncio, base64, binascii, collections, copy, dataclasses, datetime, functools, itertools, json, math, os, pathlib, random, re, sys, time, typing and unicodedata. The docs say 'Notably absent: enum, contextlib, io, string, struct, operator, inspect, logging, traceback, hashlib, uuid, urllib', and socket, subprocess, multiprocessing, threading and ctypes are absent by design. Class inheritance, metaclasses, method decorators, yield, match and del are rejected at parse time. Host functions run 'with your process's full authority', so the boundary is only as strong as what is handed in. It would complement srt only if the stack adopts code-mode tool orchestration.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run this only if a code-mode tool-call workload is selected. Run the same orchestration task set (for example N=50 model-written snippets calling the same host tool functions) in Monty and in a Python subprocess under srt. Compare task success within Monty's Python subset, p50/p95 start latency, and containment of hostile snippets (memory bomb, infinite loop, deep recursion, attempts to reach files, environment or network) with Monty's limits set. Adopt Monty for that workload only if success is within a few points of the srt arm, every hostile snippet is contained, and latency is materially lower. Any research-code workload that needs numpy or pandas fails by construction.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Tart offers a macOS-arm64 VM boundary for the M5 Pro hosts, where both winners are untested. On macOS, srt uses sandbox-exec and Codex uses Seatbelt; neither is a VM boundary. Tart was renamed from cirruslabs/tart: GraphQL resolves the old name to openai/tart. It runs macOS and Linux guests on Apple Virtualization.framework. Relevant features at 2.40.1: --dir shares with an ':ro' option over virtio-fs (Run.swift L165-176). Softnet is 'essentially a userspace packet filter'; by default the VM can send only 'to globally routable IPv4 addresses' and to the vmnet gateway (L188-200). --net-softnet-allow and --net-softnet-block take CIDRs; block wins on an equal prefix, and blocking 0.0.0.0/0 gives default deny (L208-226). Softnet needs a SUID helper (L432 configureSUIDBitIfNeeded). --net-host, which 2.40.1 moved to VMNET_HOST_MODE, requires macOS 26 (L707). Clipboard sharing can be disabled (L97). apple/container 1.5.0, already proposed in round 1, gives each container 'the isolation properties of a full VM' (technical-overview L28) and per-network isolation on macOS 26 (networking.md L155-176). An egress allow/deny filter was not found in its networking.md, technical-overview.md or how-to.md at 1.5.0. Tart's Softnet adds CIDR egress filtering (IPv4 only, no domain allowlist) and can run macOS guests, which apple/container's Linux OCI images cannot. Neither offers domain-level egress policy, so a proxy such as srt would still be needed for that. The license is FSL-1.1-ALv2 (information only).
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On an M5 Pro, run the same Linux workload fixture set in tart 2.40.1 (Softnet default deny plus an allow list) and in apple/container 1.5.0 (an isolated network). The fixtures: write outside a read-only --dir share; egress to a private-range IP, a public IP and a blocked CIDR; DNS to the host resolver; and teardown with no VM or disk residue left behind. Prefer tart only if it enforces the read-only share and the CIDR policy with no leak while container cannot express the egress policy, and its cold start and teardown are acceptable for per-task use. Prefer apple/container if both enforce equally, since its per-task OCI flow is lighter.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: libkrun, which moved from containers/libkrun (GraphQL resolves the old name), is the VMM under round-1 wrappers. The microsandbox README thanks libkrun, and smolvm's README lists its architecture as 'Library (libkrun)'. The critic's brief says gondolin also names it; that was not re-verified here. libkrun's own README defines a qualification test that no wrapper has passed here. It says 'both the guest and the VMM pertain to the same security context... Host resources that are accessible to the VMM can potentially be accessed by the guest through it', and that you must 'use the host's OS security features to run the VMM inside an isolated context' (L86-90). For virtio-fs, libkrun 'does not provide any protection against the guest attempting to access other directories in the same filesystem, or even other filesystems in the host' (L96-98), and guests can exhaust inodes and disk (L100). With TSI, 'the VMM acts as a proxy for AF_INET, AF_INET6 and AF_UNIX sockets' (L104). So a libkrun-based wrapper is a hostile-workload boundary only if it confines its VMM and applies egress policy at the VMM. BoxLite documents a Jailer (seccomp, or sandbox-exec on macOS) plus cgroups and rlimits; microsandbox and smolvm need the same check. A maintained OCI path needs no new wrapper: crun's krun handler, 'crun based OCI runtime using libkrun to run containerized programs in isolated KVM environments'. It runs as `podman run --runtime=krun`, with krun.cpus (max 16), krun.ram_mib (defaults to the OCI memory limit) and passt or TSI networking. That pairs with round-1's podman candidate, whereas Kata's Limitations.md says Kata 'does not support Podman'. A host prerequisite is unmet: /dev/kvm is crw-rw---- root:kvm and the user is not in the kvm group (nested KVM is enabled, kvm_amd nested=1).
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: First grant the user /dev/kvm access through the kvm group. Then run the gap fixtures under `podman --runtime=krun` and under one round-1 libkrun wrapper: filesystem permit/deny including a virtio-fs escape attempt outside the shared directory; egress allow/deny including IPv6 and a DNS name resolving to loopback; memory, fork and CPU bombs; and teardown residue. Verify from /proc that the VMM process runs inside its own namespaces, seccomp filter and cgroup. The VM path earns the hostile-workload slot only if every deny holds, krun.ram_mib/cpus or cgroups stop the resource bombs, and the VMM is confined. Otherwise srt plus the outer systemd cgroup stays.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The layer's next_action asks for 'one OCI/VM candidate', and Kata is the maintained OCI runtime that puts containers in a VM. The 4.2.0 notes show runtime-rs/QEMU and Dragonball work; other hypervisor backends were not verified in this lane. Compared with the round-1 candidates, Kata is the VM-per-container path for Docker Engine (moby, an existing conditional alternative) and for nerdctl: 'Docker supports Kata Containers since 22.06: sudo docker run --runtime io.containerd.kata.v2'. However, 'Currently Kata Containers does not support Podman' (Limitations.md L62-74), and host networking (--net=host) is unsupported (L105-118). Its fit for a local-first workstation is weak. The documented launch path uses sudo with Docker or containerd. A default-branch code search of Kata's markdown docs found no WSL mention. On this host, /dev/kvm (root:kvm) and /dev/vhost-vsock (root:sgx) are not accessible to the user. For a podman-centred stack, crun's krun handler (see the libkrun entry) is the closer VM path; Kata applies if Docker Engine or nerdctl is chosen as the OCI front end.

It waits for two listening sockets via /proc/net/sockstat and gives up after 0.3 s. Its upstream baseline (0-2/800 refusals quiet, 69/400 with every CPU busy, 20/20 with relays 100 ms late) differs from this host's 8/8 (2-readiness-race-quantified.json:23), so the host's failure may exceed the 0.3 s cap. The receipt's 'no upstream fix' (line 28) is now outdated. The gap stays open until N>=8 runs without retries at one pinned SHA show 0 refusals. The SHA is the merge 5766a039c4da or main head 232db177034e, built from a git checkout with the repo's own npm build (not verified here); alternatively, wait for v0.0.79.
- Gap 3 (hidden mount): documented behaviour. The v0.0.78 README L440 says a read-denied directory becomes an 'EMPTY WRITABLE directory' whose writes are lost when the command exits. A change was not found in the v0.0.78 notes or in commit titles v0.0.78...main. Whether the v0.0.77 README already said this was not checked.
- Gap 0 (network): README L355-367 documents port-scoped allowedDomains, bracketed IPv6 literals and a resolved-address check. The check covers loopback, link-local, multicast, metadata endpoints and the host's own addresses, for IPv4 and IPv6; private-use space is not denied by default. proposed.demonstrated_gap: This is the unexecuted challenger arm against a measured winner gap. No recovery advantage is claimed. In the retained 2026-09-23 comparison, Dagu 2.16.6 at its default stale-run detection failed the preregistered SIGKILL case (no scheduler, 150 s bound). It recovered only in a post-hoc scheduler variant, at 181.4 s and 182.6 s. The record says 'Dagster and Restate were not executed, so their exclusion still rests on source review'. Restate's documented semantics bear on that case. It is a single self-contained binary with no external dependencies (Homebrew and prebuilt binaries). A single node fsyncs committed data before acknowledging and loses no data on a node or process crash, with a short unavailability while it restarts. An invocation that sends no journal entries within the default 1-minute inactivity timeout is suspended and retried, and the retry policy is configurable. Cancel (graceful, progress persisted) is distinct from kill (forceful). New since the 2026-09-29 sweep: v1.7.13 (2026-10-01) and v1.8.0-rc.1 (2026-10-02), and the bundled web UI reached v1.0 in the 1.7 line. It stays at compare, not targeted, for four reasons. Handlers run in a separate service process, so process-tree bounds still come from systemd or Dagu and cancellation is cooperative. Its server-plus-service-plus-adapter shape is the operational burden that now decides Temporal's exclusion. No matched-configuration run exists. proposed.demonstrated_gap: Hatchet documents worker-loss recovery across hosts, which Dagu does not document today. Dagu issue #2805 ('support managed-session recovery after distributed worker loss') is still open. At its default stale-run detection, Dagu 2.16.6's measured SIGKILL recovery needed a running scheduler and took about 182 s. Hatchet's FAQ documents a 4-second worker heartbeat. After 30 seconds without one (a process crash including SIGKILL, a network disruption or resource pressure), the engine marks the worker inactive and re-queues its in-flight tasks for other workers. That bound is documented, not measured, and no matched-configuration run against a tuned Dagu exists. Durable tasks checkpoint at each wait (sleep, event or child run) and resume from the latest checkpoint after a worker restart or crash. Durable sleep respects its duration across interruptions. New since the 2026-09-23 trading-layer refutation: the Python SDK's embedded mode, Hatchet.from_embedded(), present by SDK v1.38.1 (2026-08-25). Cancellation is cooperative (ctx.exit_flag or ctx.cancelled), so process trees still need systemd cgroup containment. The store is Postgres. proposed.demonstrated_gap: Obelisk is the only surveyed durable engine with Dagu's footprint that also runs native host processes. It ships as one binary with embedded SQLite and an embedded web UI, with prebuilt x86_64 Linux and aarch64 macOS archives. Exec activities (since v0.38.0) run host executables and collect stdout and stderr. In v0.42.0 (2026-10-04), an exec activity's process group is killed and reaped when its lock expires or the executor shuts down, which prevents overlap with a retry (#1022). The default execution lock expiry is now 30 s, and [limits] cells cap exec processes (default 32). A crashed executor's work therefore becomes retryable through lock expiry, without a separate scheduler process. That bound is documented only. Dagu's comparable figure (about 182 s, with a scheduler required) was measured at its default stale-run detection, and no matched-configuration run exists. Bounded-tree acceptance would still come from systemd cgroup containment, the same as on the Dagu path. Workflows are WASM components or JavaScript (workflow-js), so Python research jobs would run as exec activities. It stays at compare, not targeted, for maintenance and supply-chain reasons. The README says 'Pre-release: Expect changes in CLI, gRPC, WIT, and database schema'. Each of v0.40.0, v0.41.0 and v0.42.0 carries breaking configuration, API or schema changes: 0.42 splits server.toml, requires an app name, moves the SQLite directory and stops publishing to crates.io. The contributors API lists one human contributor (tomasol, 6406 contributions); the other entries are bots.

- v262 is not like-for-like with Ubuntu's 255.4-1ubuntu8.17 package.
- systemd is a Linux service manager (not re-fetched in this sweep), so its macos-arm64 'untested' status cannot become a pass. launchd is the native analogue there and has no GitHub upstream.

No winner was archived, renamed or relicensed.

INCUMBENCY
- Dagu's recovery standing rests on local integration evidence for its tested cases. At its default stale-run detection it failed the preregistered SIGKILL case (150 s bound), and no matched-configuration comparison against a durable challenger exists.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The layer has no out-of-band detector for a missed or silent run, and two kinds of failure need one. (a) Host loss: when the WSL2 PC reboots, loses power, or its user manager crashes, Dagu and systemd stop with it. Dagu's catch-up (#1180; #2742 in v2.16.4; catchup_window inheritance fix #2770 in v2.16.6) acts only after the scheduler returns. On the Macs, Apple documents that a StartCalendarInterval job missed while the machine is powered off never runs. (b) Silent skips on a healthy host: dagucloud/dagu#2970 (closed 2026-10-03) reports a scheduled run silently skipped while any run of the DAG is queued. v2.18.2 only logs the skipped slot (#2980), so nothing alerts. Healthchecks is a dead man's switch (introduction.md L3-11). It offers Simple, Cron and OnCalendar schedules (configuring_checks.md L33; OnCalendar is systemd-timer syntax). Cron schedules take an expression, the server's time zone and a grace time (L52-67), so a weekday America/New_York market-hours job maps directly. Grace Time also bounds the gap from start to success (L39-50). /start marks a run that never finishes as down after grace and records durations (measuring_script_run_time.md L3-31, L50-53). It ships an ntfy integration (hc/integrations/ntfy). Self-hosting needs Python 3.12+ and Django 6.0, with SQLite as the default store (self_hosted.md L11-13, L57-58). Alerts are sent only while a separately supervised `sendalerts` process runs (L68-70, L148-150). Gatus heartbeats are fixed-interval and have no start/duration signal, so Healthchecks is the better semantic fit for calendar-scheduled data and research jobs and for detecting hangs.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: This is a bounded trial, and both the monitor and its alert path sit off the WSL2 host. The stack's ntfy is a loopback topic on the workstation (adoption/templates/systemd/host-requests-workstation.service L10), so a host failure would take notification down with it. The off-host alert route is part of the trial. Arms: Healthchecks, with its web process and sendalerts both supervised, against Gatus external-endpoint heartbeats as the comparison arm. Frozen cases: (1) WSL2 host powered off, or the systemd user manager killed, while a slot is due; measure time-to-alert against configured grace. (2) A slot skipped on a healthy host, reproducing the #2970 queued-run skip. (3) A /start with no finish (hang). (4) A nonzero exit. (5) A duplicate run. (6) A weekend or holiday gap for a weekday cron job; count false alerts. (7) Restart of the monitor host; check retained state and history. Metrics: detection latency, false alerts, history kept per check, off-host alert delivery, and the processes and memory needed to operate. Healthchecks is overturned if Gatus detects cases 1-4 with equal latency and no more false alerts at lower operating cost, or if Healthchecks misses case 2 or 3.

It manages services with launchctl on macOS and systemctl on Linux (Library/Homebrew/cmd/services.rb L15-16). With sudo it uses /Library/LaunchDaemons, started at boot; otherwise it uses ~/Library/LaunchAgents, started at login (L18-19). `--sudo-service-user` runs the service as a named user when root starts it (L27-28), and per-formula env files persist across upgrades (L21-25). homebrew-core's dagu formula (Formula/d/dagu.rb @74893e2d, 2026-10-04) already declares `service do run [opt_bin/"dagu", "start-all"]; keep_alive true; log_path/error_log_path var/"log/dagu.log"; working_dir var` (L37-42). A StartCalendarInterval slot missed while powered off is never run (Apple ScheduledJobs). proposed.demonstrated_gap: The layer records no native scheduling surface for agent-run (model) workloads, although claude-code is in its components_vs_upstream. The installed client (2.1.291) has three. (1) /loop and the cron tools are session-scoped. Recurring tasks expire after 7 days (official docs; a third-party search summary saying 3 days is wrong). They fire only while the REPL is idle, run up to 10% of the period late (max 15 min), and in this worker session the CronCreate schema says 'durable' has no effect. (2) Desktop scheduled tasks run on the local machine while the app is open. Their 'Review history' lists every past run, including skipped runs with the reason (asleep, previous run still in progress, other tasks running), and tasks can be paused, resumed and deleted. (3) Routines run in Anthropic's cloud. They are a research preview, start from a fresh clone with no local files, run at most hourly, and are subject to hourly caps and subscription usage. Their list_runs history omits fires skipped before a session existed (RemoteTrigger schema). Only routines survive loss of the WSL2 host, and they cannot reach local data or research state, so none of the three closes the host-failure gap for local workloads. Desktop's skipped-run history is something a Dagu-run `claude -p` job does not record natively. Reliability is still moving. 2.1.290 fixed extra runs on resume, respawn or fork; tasks that never fired after a /background hand-off; tasks lost after compaction; and wakeups silently lost when background sessions were restarted through updates and low memory (CHANGELOG L28-29, L133, L164). 2.1.274 fixed a routine firing twice after an edit (L1534). Remote-provider cancellation and when billing stops were not found in the scheduled-tasks or routines docs or in the v2.1.291 changelog, so that open gap stays open.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Schedule one real agent job, for example a daily research summary over a fixed repository, three ways: a Dagu DAG step running headless `claude -p` (the current path), a Claude Desktop scheduled task on an M5 Pro, and a routine. Inject sleep and power-off across a slot, a cancellation mid-run, a resume or respawn, and an edit to the schedule. Score whether every skipped or duplicate run is recorded with its cause, cancellation latency, whether the local process tree and the remote model run (billing) stop, usage accounting, and lines of glue. A native surface replaces Dagu for agent jobs only if it records every skipped or duplicate run and stops runs cleanly with less glue. Otherwise Dagu keeps scheduling and the native surfaces stay conveniences.

followup_reason.reason:
All eight proposals are durable-execution engines or schedulers, a class known_repositories already saturates. The open gaps are elsewhere: host failure (reboot, power loss, a host or user-manager crash, recovery on an independent host) and the lack of any real workload.

Three classes are absent from all 32 inputs.
1. External heartbeat or dead-man's-switch monitoring, which still detects a missed or silent run when the scheduling host itself fails:
   - https://github.com/healthchecks/healthchecks: v4.4, 2026-08-31; commit 2026-10-06.
   - https://github.com/TwiN/gatus: v5.37.0, 2026-09-24.
   - https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma: 2.5.5, 2026-09-16; push monitors.
2. A macOS supervisor. The slot is empty, not merely untested. systemd is 'a suite of basic building blocks for a Linux system' (https://systemd.io/), Apple's supervisor is launchd (https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html), and scheduling-supervision.json never mentions launchd.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: No container on the 2604 host can use the RTX 4090 today. Docker Engine is installed (docker-ce 5:29.8.2), but nvidia-ctk and nvidia-container-cli are absent. The Windows driver's libcuda.so and nvidia-smi are present under /usr/lib/wsl/lib (read-only host check, 2026-10-06). This is not yet a requirement. docs/new-wsl-handbook.md:971 records the gpu-container-runtime slot (foundation/hosting-services/added) as resolved but not installed, because 'no settled owner runs GPU work in a container (the model server and the document parser install natively)'. The same row names this toolkit as the default once an owner does. v1.20.1 (2026-09-19) is the vendor's current release. On WSL2, NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=none now prevents GPU injection (PR #2025). crun with user namespaces no longer hits rootfs permission errors, which matters for rootless use (PR #1971). `nvidia-ctk runtime configure` now keeps existing Docker feature flags when enabling CDI (PR #2049). The 1.20.1 docs say the runtime selects JIT-CDI automatically on WSL2. NVIDIA's CUDA on WSL guide lists the Docker CLI and Docker Desktop as supported and forbids installing a Linux GPU driver inside WSL2.

Run nvidia-smi -L, then the same inference image digest, model weights and workload as the native server. Adopt if the container shows the host GPU UUID and, over repeated trials, throughput and peak memory stay within a pre-registered margin of native. Keep native if the margin fails or the workload needs full Unified Memory, which WSL2 lacks.

claude_discover.notes:
SCOPE. This follow-up round covered three classes the container lane needs but no input contained: image supply chain, GPU containers and PostgreSQL currency. It also reconciled the macOS-arm64 status. None of the seven first-round repositories was re-proposed.

SEEDED ITEMS NOT PROPOSED
(1) https://github.com/docker-hardened-images/keyring is not proposed as a standalone candidate. It has no default-branch commit since 2026-07-08 (the gh api commits?since query returned none; pushed_at 2026-03-25T19:07:33Z), so the Scorecard-derived rule makes it stale as a standalone repository. It is a static public-key store, and Docker also publishes the key at https://registry.scout.docker.com/keyring/dhi/latest.pub (docs.docker.com/dhi/how-to/verify.md). The DHI trial should fetch the key from both places and compare them before verifying.
(2) https://github.com/postgres/postgres is a winner, not a candidate; its currency follows.

POSTGRESQL CURRENCY (winner health)
- REL_18_6 is a lightweight tag on commit 724edf9bde9d ('Stamp 18.6.', 2026-08-11T18:38:31Z). It is the newest 18.x tag.
- There is no REL_18_5. The 18.6 release notes (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/release-18-6.html, release date 2026-08-13) say '18.5 was never released, due to a regression discovered post-wrap'.
- The same notes list post-update work: configuration adjustments and data cleanups (first three security entries, including the new output_plugin_libraries setting, which pg_upgrade --check enforces), a GIN reltuples check and reindexing for btree_gist and ltree. Whether the 18.6 fixture applied these was not checked here.
- PostgreSQL 19 has only REL_19_BETA1 to BETA4 (all lightweight tags). REL_19_BETA4 is commit b73d13c32c83 ('Stamp 19beta4.', 2026-09-21T19:15:09Z). Neither REL_19_RC1 nor REL_19_0 existed on 2026-10-06.
- The Beta 4 announcement (https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/postgresql-19-beta-4-3386/, 2026-09-24) says the RC 'should occur in early October', GA 'may also occur in October', several features were reverted, and upgrading needs pg_upgrade or dump/restore.
- DHI has no PostgreSQL 19 definition yet (debian-13 covers 14 to 18).
- Qualification plan, after REL_19_0 and the GA announcement exist:
  1. Build 19.0 from the blueprint's hash-pinned source archive.
  2. Run pg_upgrade --check, then pg_upgrade, from an 18.6 cluster holding the fixture data.
  3. Run make verify, restart persistence, migration up/down/up and the backup/restore receipt, and compare each with the 18.6 baseline.
  Never pin a beta or RC.

TAG-ONLY CURRENCY CHECK
- components_vs_upstream shows latest=None for postgresql because tools/sota-convergence/build_manifest.py:263-270 flags the repos/{slug}/tags?per_page=1 fallback ('release-6-3').
- The existing runtime tag declaration (RUNTIME_TAG_KEYS prefix/pattern at tools/sota-convergence/extract_layers.py:335; select_matching_tag at build_manifest.py:552) does not fix this as it stands. select_matching_tag requires the captured version to match DOTTED_VERSION_RE (build_manifest.py:546, dotted digits), and PostgreSQL tags use underscores (REL_18_6).
- A declaration therefore needs prefix 'REL_' plus underscore-to-dot normalization (or an accepted underscore capture), and must exclude BETA and RC names.
- This is a glue change for the coordinator; this read-only lane made no edit.

macOS-ARM64 RECONCILIATION: the receipt does not qualify.
- evidence/artifacts/macos-application-20260924/run-summary.json is a run artifact. Platform status counts only host receipts under evidence/hosts/ (scripts/platform_status.py docstring).
- The matching host receipts are evidence/hosts/macos-m5pro-20260924/macos-m5pro-20260924--{fastapi,nextjs,postgresql}--use--20260924.json. They are bound native_proven use passes at 0.141.1, 16.3.5 and 18.6, recorded on a declared second physical machine.
- Each has two agree reviews and a standing independent dissent: agent-lab-e9, workflow wf_f7021e8d-fd3, native-agent-stack#201 comment 5818957285, 'needs_changes; reproducing the commands does not establish that they exercise the layer role, a positive control or the pin'.
- platform_status() (scripts/platform_status.py:159), run at HEAD ecfa112764c6 over the winners in catalogs/landscape/foundation.json, derives macos-arm64 = not_established for all three, with the reason 'host receipts at pin ... but none passes without a standing dissent'.
- The declared 'untested' comes from the verdict sealed on 2026-09-22, before the receipts of 2026-09-24. It should read not_established at the next re-record.
- The run summary also records attempt 11 (restart persistence and migration rollback) with exit 1. The script's own post-SIGTERM bind probe found a TIME_WAIT socket on port 18081, although every functional check passed.
- To qualify, a new Mac use receipt must:
  - be recorded at the current pins (the stack now installs nextjs 16.3.8, so the 16.3.5 receipt stops binding once the verdict re-records);
  - include a positive control that exercises the layer role (the app's API and browser tests against the database) and evidence of the pin;
  - pass an independent review with no dissent, then supersede the dissented receipts.

STANDING THAT RESTS ON INCUMBENCY OR DOCUMENTED FIT RATHER THAN CURRENT EVIDENCE
- The same derivation gives linux-wsl2-x86_64 = conditional for nextjs and postgresql ('native_proven winner without a registered evidence/ reference'), while the layer input declares them accepted. Only fastapi derives accepted, from evidence/hosts/nativestack-5975wx-20260925/nativestack-5975wx-20260925--fastapi--use--20260926-2.json.
- The container-engine slot (Docker Engine/Moby) is kept on 'default on documented fit; nothing measured separates the finalists' (docs/new-wsl-handbook.md:970).
- Other winner health, taken from the layer input and not re-fetched here: fastapi pin 0.141.1 is behind 0.142.2 (2026-09-30); the nextjs verdict pin is 16.3.5 while the installed and upstream version is 16.3.8. No winner is archived, renamed or relicensed.

STAR SCAN. The star-candidates.json entries that touch this layer are docker/awesome-compose (examples that upstream says are not for production), veggiemonk/awesome-docker (a directory) and supabase/supabase (outside_north_star). beyond_stars lists sigstore/cosign, which is already cataloged as 'cosign' and is the verification tool both the DHI and the Chainguard arms need. None was proposed.

LIMITS
- The docs read in this lane confirm signed SBOM and provenance attestations for DHI. They do not confirm the DHI SLSA build level or VEX attestation types.
- The SBOM and signature properties of an apko-built image were not checked.
- Whether the operator already holds a Docker ID is unknown; no credential store was read.
- The supply-chain-risk-auditor collector was not run, because the targets are OCI image catalogs, not npm, PyPI or Go manifests of this project. Its reading rules were applied: unassessable is not risk, and figures are quoted as measured.
- search-first was not invoked, because the user's CLAUDE.md reserves it for a coordinator.
- The advisor was rate-limited and gave no review.
- Budget used: 37 gh api calls (counted per invocation), 5 web searches and 8 page fetches; the page-fetch budget is exhausted.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Reopen of the 2026-09-29 proposal with corrected facts. The gap is automatic recovery of a warm keep-alive CLI bridge after its long-lived process dies unexpectedly. The winner documents that it does not recover this way, and this stack has measured it. mcporter docs/daemon.md L36 at v0.14.2 says: 'An unexpected daemon-process exit leaves metadata that blocks automatic replacement: an operator must verify its transports have retired before clearing stale state.' The gap-wave2 receipts record a refused call and auto_recovered false after SIGKILL on 0.13.13 (2-owned-daemon-lifecycle-stages.json) and on 0.14.0 (raw/lifecycle-mcporter-0.14.0.json, where the manual step was archiving daemon/user.json). mcpc documents the opposite for its session bridge. It auto-reconnects on network failures or its own crashes, with a 10 s cooldown on failed retries. It has a 'crashed' state, 'Bridge process crashed or was killed; auto-reconnects in the background', and it has clean and clean all (README L405-L427 at 8416cc8bc7b3). Its --proxy exposes one session and 'serves protocol 2025-11-25 to its clients' (README L580-L585). `mcporter serve` answers both 2026-07-28 and 2025-era clients (CHANGELOG 0.13.0). Both tools speak 2026-07-28 (mcpc README L890; mcporter CHANGELOG L236). proposed.demonstrated_gap: Reopen with new evidence. The gap: nothing checks the bridge or the installed servers per protocol revision under the breaking 2026-07-28 revision. MCP 2026-07-28 (spec release tag 2026-07-28) is stateless. The conformance README says revisions through 2025-11-25 use the stateful initialize handshake, while 2026-07-28 is stateless with per-request _meta. A scenario that belongs to both revisions must therefore run once per revision, and 'Passing it on one wire says nothing about the other' (README L121-L170 at c37eec888e1c). mcporter claims both generations, including `mcporter serve` answering 2026-07-28 and 2025-era clients through one endpoint (CHANGELOG 0.13.0 at v0.14.2). Each version is unique and immutable once published (versioning.mdx L32). Range strings are rejected (L44-66). Inspector 2.9.0, a winner, already parses registry server.json against schema 2025-12-11 (core/mcp/import/serverJson.ts L2, L13), the latest dated schema (server-json CHANGELOG L39). Hosted prod reports 1.8.1, which carries the github.io org-namespace takeover fix (#1506). The gate covers provenance only, not safety: a keyword search of the README, versioning, requirements and authentication docs at v1.8.1 found no behaviour or safety review. A name search is itself the unexamined-entry trap, as the hosted registry showed. Searching chrome-devtools-mcp returned io.github.Async23/chrome-devtools-mcp first (npm @async23/chrome-devtools-mcp 1.7.0, isLatest true), with the official title and description. The upstream release chrome-devtools-mcp-v1.10.1 is dated 2026-09-23T10:37:16Z. Risks: the registry is still preview, and breaking changes or data resets may occur (authentication.mdx L7). Its own ownership checks had five advisories, all fixed by 1.7.9, including GHSA-2v5f-5r6w-p67r (OCI ownership check skipped) and GHSA-95c3-6vvw-4mrq (OIDC token replay). proposed.demonstrated_gap: The winners carry no SEP-414 trace context. The 2026-07-28 changelog documents traceparent, tracestate and baggage in _meta (changelog.mdx L33). mcporter has no traceparent in GitHub code search (0 files) and none in CHANGELOG.md@v0.14.2. A tool call bridged by mcporter therefore cannot join an OpenTelemetry trace. agentgateway v1.6.0 copies the W3C trace keys into every upstream MCP message's _meta (crates/agentgateway/src/mcp/upstream/mod.rs L115-118, applied at L347 and L404, unit test L887-900). In v1.6.0, CEL policies can match mcp.methodName such as tools/call, and RBAC evaluation populates it (#3197). The release also adds SSE keep-alive on long-lived MCP streams. Serving both modern (2026-07-28) and legacy clients (upstream/mod.rs L177, L465) is only parity: `mcporter serve` already bridges both eras (mcporter CHANGELOG L239). The trial is feasible on both hosts without a cluster: standalone agentgateway-linux-amd64 and agentgateway-darwin-arm64 binaries ship with .sha256 files. Maintenance is high, with 775 default-branch commits since 2026-07-08. Advisory status is unassessed: the GitHub Advisory Database has no package under RUST/agentgateway. Its role would be a complement in front of the bridged servers, not a replacement for mcporter's CLI and codegen.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Put the same local servers behind `mcporter serve` and behind standalone agentgateway v1.6.0. Drive both with a 2025-11-25 client and a 2026-07-28 client (Claude Code 2.1.291 or codex 0.160.1). Measure four things. (a) tools/list and tools/call parity. (b) Whether the inbound traceparent reaches the upstream server's _meta, captured by a local OTel collector. (c) Whether a CEL deny rule on one tool blocks only that tool. (d) Recovery after the upstream process is killed, timed against the mcporter daemon. If (b) or (c) fails, or calls regress, agentgateway is not adopted. If mcporter ships SEP-414 propagation, the gap closes.
