proposed.demonstrated_gap: Neither M5 Pro Mac has a qualified optional generation route. Every winner and the llama.cpp trial route are 'untested' on macos-arm64 (layer input platform_status). The 2026-09-29 sweep left mlx-lm not adjudicated only because a vote did not return. mlx-lm is the vendor-org engine (ml-explore, Apple). Apple benchmarked the M5 GPU Neural Accelerators with it on a 24 GB MacBook Pro with the base M5; these hosts are M5 Pro. MLX reaches the accelerators through Metal 4 TensorOps and Metal Performance Primitives and needs macOS 26.2 or later. The control's equivalent path is newer and still moving. llama.cpp enabled the Metal 4.0 tensor API on M5+ in b10734 (2026-09-01). v0.6.0 (b11429, 2026-10-05) then added a tensor-API flash-attention kernel and few-row MMA kernels, both beyond the stack pin b11057. So it is unanswered which engine gives better TTFT, decode speed, memory use and oracle agreement on M5 Pro. A trial is feasible now, because main ships server.py, SERVER.md and benchmark.py for a server-to-server comparison with llama-server. It is maintained: 126 default-branch commits since 2026-07-08, and no published advisories. Its latest GitHub release object is v0.31.3, but a v0.32.0 tag points at a commit dated 2026-09-30.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On the 64 GB M5 Pro (macOS 26.2 or later), serve the same 4-bit model tier with each engine, for example the models layer's conditional Qwen3.8-27B. Run mlx_lm.server (v0.32.0) against llama-server at v0.6.0/b11429 or later with the Metal tensor API active. Measure TTFT at a 4,096-token prompt, decode t/s over 128 or more tokens, peak unified memory, frozen repair oracle pass rate and output agreement, and recovery after kill -9 and restart. Repeat with a smaller quant on the 24 GB Mac. mlx-lm becomes the Mac route only if it beats llama-server by 15% or more on TTFT or decode, at an equal oracle pass rate and within the memory budget. Otherwise llama.cpp stays the single cross-host route and mlx-lm drops to keep_but_compare. Add Ollama's MLX runtime as a third arm once v0.40.0 is a stable release.

Its core function is on-demand load and unload of several models behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The control route now does that natively. llama-server router mode is documented at the stack pin b11057: it 'exposes an API for dynamically loading and unloading models', with --models-dir, --models-max (default 4) and per-model /metrics?model=. Master also documents --models-preset and --models-autoload, and v0.6.0 continues router fixes. Two things remain unique to llama-swap. It can swap across runtimes on the single 24 GB RTX 4090, for example the vLLM embedding server and llama-server generation, using its swap-matrix DSL and ttl unload. It also serves a /metrics endpoint with system and GPU series. No VRAM-contention failure between the accepted vLLM embedding service and the llama.cpp trial is on record, so no gap is demonstrated today. It is maintained: v262 on 2026-10-03, newest commit 2026-10-03, and no published advisories.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Trigger: the local-inference plan's free-VRAM guard refuses or stops a generation arm, or an OOM occurs, because the vLLM embedding service holds memory. Then run one workload window on the 4090 two ways. Arm (a) is llama-swap v262 with vLLM and llama-server in one swap matrix with ttl. Arm (b) is llama-server router mode plus systemd stop/start of the embedding unit. Measure swap latency, OOM and refusal counts, embedding-service availability during generation, and recovery after kill -9. Adopt llama-swap only if it removes the failures without adding a capture path. Its /metrics GPU series must either match nvidia_gpu_exporter's field coverage or make that exporter redundant.

claude_discover.notes:
WINNER HEALTH (GitHub API, 2026-10-06). None of the three winners is archived, renamed or relicensed.
- opentelemetry-collector-contrib: pin 0.161.0 against upstream v0.162.0 (2026-09-29); 1,446 default-branch commits since 2026-07-08. Two breaking changes in v0.162.0 touch this stack (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/releases/tag/v0.162.0).
  - pkg/prometheus promotes PermissiveLabelSanitization to beta, on by default. It may change the label names the stack's prometheus exporter emits (collector.yaml exporters). Re-run the reconciliation queries after upgrading, or opt out with --feature-gates=-pkg.translator.prometheus.PermissiveLabelSanitization.
  - processor/transform removes the stable defaultErrorModeIgnore gate. No --feature-gates flag appears anywhere under observability/, so startup is unaffected.
- Prometheus: the sealed verdict lists 3.14.0, but the installed pin is 3.15.0, which equals upstream v3.15.0 (2026-09-25); 733 commits since 2026-07-08.
- Loki: v3.7.8 (2026-09-17) is the newest of the six latest releases, and none of them is a prerelease; 1,100 commits since 2026-07-08; license AGPL-3.0, information only.

INCUMBENCY. All three winners carry only 'synthetic' evidence_class and are 'untested' on macOS. Loki has one recorded measured point: 300/300 lines held across kill -9 and restore, per the 2026-09-26 fit vote in catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260926.json. The collector and Prometheus have no measured head-to-head on record, so their standing rests partly on incumbency.

NATIVE FINDINGS, verified.
- Claude Code beta tracing predates pin 2.1.284 (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): TRACEPARENT reaches Bash subprocesses since 2.1.97/2.1.98, SDK sessions read it since 2.1.110, and agent span parenting landed in 2.1.145. Spans redact prompt and tool content by default (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage#traces-beta). So the 2026-09-26 Jaeger and 2026-09-29 Tempo fit refutations stand.
- Jaeger v2.22.0 (2026-10-06) only changes Elasticsearch storage and span ordering (https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/releases/tag/v2.22.0). It has 2 historical advisories (2023 UI XSS, 2024 Go stdlib). Not re-proposed.
- The null path both refutations demanded is still unapplied. Claude Code attaches prompt.id to every event of one prompt (monitoring-usage#event-correlation-attributes), but prompt.id is absent from the transform/privacy log keep_keys (observability/collector/collector.yaml:233). Adding that one key is the native next step for task attribution, before any trace store.
- The Codex config reference defaults otel.metrics_exporter to statsig (https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference). The stack's codex.toml.example routes logs and metrics to local OTLP and sets trace_exporter = "none", which is consistent with one local pipeline.

COMPONENT DRIFT.
- agentsview: pin 0.43.0 against v0.44.0 (2026-09-21). Its config loader now rejects unknown keys under [vector], so check the config before upgrading (https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/releases/tag/v0.44.0).
- llama.cpp now uses semver releases. v0.6.0 (2026-10-05) maps to nightly b11429. Pin b11057 lacks the Metal tensor-API flash-attention kernel and the few-row MMA kernels.
- vLLM: pin 0.30.0 against v0.31.0 (2026-10-05). Breaking changes: quantization="fp8" online quantization is replaced by fp8_per_tensor, and tokenizer_mode="slow" is removed. Check the embedding unit's flags (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.31.0).
- claude-code: pin 2.1.284; installed 2.1.291 equals upstream latest; 2.1.288 fixed tool.blocked_on_user spans in -p and SDK sessions.

CHECKED, NOT PROPOSED.
- VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs v1.53.0 (2026-10-01) and VictoriaMetrics v1.153.0: active, but both were refuted on fit on 2026-09-26, and there is no new evidence since.
- grafana/alloy v1.20.1, grafana/docker-otel-lgtm v0.35.0, SigNoz/signoz v0.145.0, hyperdxio/hyperdx and CtrlSpice/otel-desktop-viewer v0.5.0: active by GraphQL history only. None shows a gap against the winners or against otel-tui.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: This is a model-level, newest-technique gap on the stack's own qualified route, and it needs no new component. The frozen WSL RTX 4090 route (native-agent-stack@ecfa1127 blueprints/convergence-practice/gpu-inference/plan.json) runs without speculative decoding. It uses b11057, Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M, partial offload at 32 GPU layers, temperature 0 with top_k 1, and a latency_rule that reports cold load, first content and generation separately. DSpark extends DFlash with a semi-autoregressive Markov head, so each draft forward pass emits a whole block. It is documented as '--spec-type draft-dspark' in docs/speculative.md, and that file is byte-identical at the stack's pin b11057 and at v0.6.0 (diffed). common/arg.cpp at b11057 already handles COMMON_SPECULATIVE_TYPE_DRAFT_DSPARK (L378-380). This corrects the critic's premise: DSpark needs no pin bump. Speculative decoding is 'exact under greedy decoding' (LFM2.5-VL-3B-DSpark card), which matches the route's greedy settings, so the 12-test oracle should be unaffected while generation time may fall; the size of the gain under partial offload is a hypothesis to measure. The drafter is the constraint. llama.cpp says 'Currently only drafts with a Qwen3 backbone are supported', and the Qwen3.8-27B DSpark drafters from the last two weeks are community speculators-format uploads (for example inference-optimization/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark-FP8-DYNAMIC, 2026-09-28). No Qwen-org drafter appears among the 60 newest DSpark repositories. v0.6.0 (2026-10-05) matters for a Mac arm: it adds few-row MMA Metal kernels for speculative and batched decoding (#29869) and probabilistic sampling for simple draft and MTP (#27694).
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Gate: at b11057, convert one Qwen3.8-27B DSpark drafter with 'convert_hf_to_gguf.py --target-model-dir' as docs/speculative.md describes. If conversion or the Qwen3-backbone restriction fails, record the drafter as unsupported at b11057 and v0.6.0 and stop. Otherwise run an A/B in the same host state, at least 3 runs each: the frozen plan unchanged vs the frozen plan plus '-md <drafter.gguf> --spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max <block>'. Pass if all of the following hold: the text matches the no-draft baseline at temperature 0; the oracle passes 12/12; generation time improves by a margin declared in advance; VRAM stays within the plan's admission budget; and the server recovers after a restart. Refute on low acceptance (no gain), divergent output, or a VRAM admission failure. A Mac arm can repeat the run with Qwen/Qwen3-4B plus deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7 (the pair the docs name) on Metal, comparing b11057 with v0.6.0.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Decisive reason: the data-path objection that refuted phoenix applies unchanged, and the content switch is weaker than the pipeline's guarantee. (1) OpenLLMetry is trace-first. 'By default, OpenLLMetry logs prompts, completions, and embeddings to span attributes', and only TRACELOOP_TRACE_CONTENT=false turns this off. The stack's collector defines logs, metrics, metrics/health, logs/sdk_receipts and metrics/host pipelines, and no traces pipeline (collector.yaml L315-335). (2) Traceloop's doc says every instrumentation respects the flag, yet the 0.62.4 changelog fixes 'mcp: honor TRACELOOP_TRACE_CONTENT on the client path (#4466)'. So the off switch was not honored on at least one path until 2026-09-29. (3) The collector's documented SDK-lane usage gap exists because Codex ThreadTokenUsage is cumulative and has no baseline, so transform/sdk_receipt deletes numeric usage (collector.yaml L59-74). That usage is produced inside the Codex CLI, which a Python LLM-SDK instrumentation cannot observe. Native Claude and Codex OTLP already feed the metrics pipeline. The 2026-09-26 sweep's not_adopted held, and nothing in 0.62.4 changes these facts. Maintenance itself is strong.
